title: Metabolic Risk Factors of Developing Liver Steatosis among Patients with Chronic Hepatitis B: A National Cohort from Romania

analysis.research_question_and_background: The coexistence of liver steatosis in patients with chronic viral hepatitis B (CHB) is growing relevant as the global epidemic of obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). analysis.main_results: 5,321 individuals (1.67%) were found with CHB in the screening program. analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: In our study we found a prevalence of hepatic steatosis of 42.2% in the cohort of vulnerable untreated patients with CHB, and the prevalence of severe fibrosis was 17.1%.

analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on transient elastography for diagnosing liver steatosis and the exclusion of individuals with heavy alcohol consumption or other liver diseases. analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the metabolic risk factors associated with liver steatosis in patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) in Romania. title: Risk-based hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance thresholds using a prediction score in Asian patients with chronic hepatitis B: a nationwide cohort study

analysis.research_question_and_background: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains a leading cause of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), yet surveillance strategies are often based on cirrhosis rather than individualized risk. analysis.study_design_and_population: A nationwide population-based cohort study was conducted using the Korean National Health Insurance Service database. Adults with CHB initiating nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy between 2012 and 2023 were included, while those with viral coinfections, prior malignancy, or decompensated cirrhosis were excluded.
analysis.methods: HCC risk was stratified using the HCC-RESCUE score, and incident HCC was the primary outcome. Annual HCC incidence rates and adjusted hazard ratios were estimated using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models.
analysis.main_results: Among 199,143 treated patients (median follow-up, 7.3 years), 15,233 developed HCC. Adjusted annual HCC incidence increased progressively across risk strata: 0.31% (95% CI 0.24–0.40) in the low-risk group, 1.09% (0.84–1.41) in the intermediate-risk group, and 1.85% (1.44–2.40) in the high-risk group.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as demonstrating a graded spectrum of residual HCC risk in antiviral-treated CHB patients and identified incidence-aligned thresholds relevant to surveillance. The novelty lies in linking HCC-RESCUE score thresholds to specific annual incidence cut-offs for surveillance guidance.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support incidence-informed refinement of HCC surveillance strategies that complement traditional cirrhosis-based criteria in the antiviral treatment era, potentially improving early detection and resource allocation.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s limitations include its reliance on a single national database and the exclusion of patients with viral coinfections or prior malignancy, which may limit generalisability. The evidence is rated as high due to the large cohort, robust statistical methods, and clear risk stratification.

analysis.summary_en: This nationwide cohort study in antiviral-treated Asian patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) quantified hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) incidence across HCC-RESCUE score-defined risk strata and derived surveillance-relevant incidence thresholds. Hazard ratios for HCC were 3.48 and 5.90 in intermediate- and high-risk groups compared to low-risk, respectively. Score thresholds corresponding to annual incidence cut-offs of 0.2%, 1.5%, and 3.0% were identified as 47, 66, and 90. The authors conclude that prediction score-based stratification reveals a graded spectrum of residual HCC risk and supports incidence-informed surveillance strategies beyond traditional cirrhosis-based criteria.

title: Genomic and transcriptomic features of HBV integration in treatment-naïve, HBeAg-positive children with chronic HBV infection

analysis.research_question_and_background: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection in children poses unique challenges for cure, yet the landscape of HBV integration and local immune responses to transcriptionally active viral integration in this population remains poorly understood.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study performed genomic analyses using a probe-based capture strategy on 18 children and 28 adults with chronic HBV infection, and spatial transcriptomics on 12 children from the cohort and 3 adults from a public database.
analysis.methods: Genomic analyses were conducted using a probe-based capture strategy, and spatial transcriptomics was performed to assess transcriptional activity and immune cell profiles.
analysis.main_results: Children exhibited significantly lower clonal expansion of HBV-integrated hepatocytes than adults despite comparable unique breakpoint counts, and transcriptionally active viral integration spots were sparsely distributed and accounted for a low proportion of all spots in children.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Children showed reduced adaptive immune cells but increased innate components and APC co-stimulation at transcriptionally active integration spots, contrasting with adults who exhibited uniform reduction of immune cell populations, offering new insights into age-related differences in HBV integration and immune response.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight age-dependent differences in HBV integration and immune microenvironment, which may inform strategies for monitoring and treating chronic HBV infection in children.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Age was identified as an independent risk factor for total frequency of unique integration breakpoints, indicating potential confounding and limiting generalisability beyond the studied cohort.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated HBV integration and local immune responses in treatment-naïve, HBeAg-positive children with chronic HBV infection compared to adults. Spatially, transcriptionally active viral integration was sparsely distributed in children, where adaptive immune cells were reduced while innate components and antigen-presenting cell co-stimulation were increased. These age-dependent differences in HBV integration and immune microenvironment provide new insights into the distinct clinical course of chronic HBV infection in children and may guide future surveillance and therapeutic strategies.

title: Comprehensive evaluation of the αβ-TCR repertoire profile in hepatitis B vaccine-positive responders and patients with chronic hepatitis B

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand the TCR repertoire characteristics in individuals with different HBV infection and vaccination statuses, as T cells play a vital role in HBV infection, mediating both protective immunity and immunopathology.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study was conducted comparing 6 inoculation-positive responders to HepB vaccination, 6 individuals with chronic hepatitis B, and 5 healthy donors, focusing on the TCR α-chain (TRA) and β-chain (TRB) repertoires in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs).
analysis.methods: High-throughput sequencing (HTS) was used to profile the TRA and TRB CDR3 repertoires in PBMCs from the three groups, with systematic comparisons of frequency, diversity, similarity, and V/J segment usage.
analysis.main_results: The CHB group showed significantly fewer unique TRA and TRB CDR3s compared to the IPR and HD groups. The BUB index for TRAV was significantly higher in IPR than in CHB and HD groups (P = 0.0073 and P = 0.0317, respectively), while for TRBV, a significantly higher BUB index was observed only between IPR and CHB groups (P = 0.0002).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings delineate distinct CDR3 repertoire characteristics of circulating T cells in IPR and CHB, offering insights into the protective response to HepB vaccination and informing future investigations into TRA- and TRB-based strategies for HBV diagnosis and prevention.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results may enhance understanding of the immune response to HepB vaccination and contribute to the development of TRA- and TRB-based strategies for HBV diagnosis and prevention.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its small sample size and abstract-only evidence, which may affect the generalisability of the findings. The evidence strength is moderate due to the lack of detailed statistical analyses and controls.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the TCR repertoire profiles in individuals with different HBV infection and vaccination statuses. It compared 6 inoculation-positive responders to HepB vaccination, 6 individuals with chronic hepatitis B, and 5 healthy donors using high-throughput sequencing. The results showed that the CHB group had fewer unique TRA and TRB CDR3s than the IPR and HD groups. The BUB index for TRAV was significantly higher in IPR than in CHB and HD groups, while for TRBV, a significantly higher BUB index was observed only between IPR and CHB groups. These findings highlight distinct TCR repertoire characteristics in IPR and CHB, which may improve understanding of the protective response to HepB vaccination and guide future research on TRA- and TRB-based strategies for HBV diagnosis and prevention. However, the study's small sample size and abstract-only evidence limit the confidence in its conclusions, suggesting a moderate evidence strength.

analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Serological screening was performed in 38.3% of patients, and 5.45% had positive test results for at least one sexually transmitted infection. The findings suggest that routine screening for sexually transmitted infections, including hepatitis B virus, is necessary in this population, as many do not undergo such testing. However, the study does not provide detailed data on the prevalence or impact of hepatitis B virus specifically, highlighting a need for further research and targeted interventions in this group.

title: siRNA daplusiran/tomligisiran and DNA vaccine JNJ-64300535 in NA-suppressed chronic hepatitis B: the OSPREY study

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to assess whether reducing viral antigens with daplusiran/tomligisiran (DAP/TOM) could enhance HBV-specific T-cell and/or HBsAg responses to the DNA vaccine JNJ-0535 in participants with virologically suppressed, HBeAg-negative chronic hepatitis B.
analysis.study_design_and_population: OSPREY was a single-arm, open-label, phase 1b study involving 24 participants with virologically suppressed, HBeAg-negative chronic hepatitis B. All participants received DAP/TOM (200 mg, Q4W) for 24 weeks and 4 doses of JNJ-0535 from Week 14 to Week 26.
analysis.methods: Participants received nucleos(t)ide analog (NA) therapy until Week 36 and continued to follow-up at Week 48 unless stopping criteria were met. The study evaluated HBsAg reduction and T-cell responses to the DNA vaccine JNJ-0535.
analysis.main_results: Of the 24 participants enrolled, 11 (45.8%) achieved the primary endpoint of ≥2 log10 HBsAg reduction at Week 36. Seven participants stopped NA based on Week 36 results and had more polyfunctional CD4 T-cells targeting ≥2 HBV antigens and a greater mean reduction in HBsAg at Follow-up Week 48 versus those who continued NA (2.42 log10 IU/mL vs 0.96 log10 IU/mL).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that JNJ-0535 vaccination may enhance core/polymerase-specific T-cell responses in some participants, with a notable difference in HBsAg reduction observed between those who stopped NA and those who continued.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide insights into the potential of combining DAP/TOM with DNA vaccines to improve immune responses in patients with suppressed chronic hepatitis B, which could inform future vaccine development strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was a single-arm, open-label trial with a small sample size, limiting the generalisability of the findings. The evidence is moderate due to the lack of a control group and the observational nature of the follow-up.

analysis.summary_en: The OSPREY study investigated whether reducing viral antigens with daplusiran/tomligisiran (DAP/TOM) could enhance HBV-specific T-cell and HBsAg responses to the DNA vaccine JNJ-0535 in participants with virologically suppressed, HBeAg-negative chronic hepatitis B. Twenty-four participants received DAP/TOM for 24 weeks and four doses of JNJ-0535 from Week 14 to Week 26. Eleven participants (45.8%) achieved a ≥2 log10 HBsAg reduction at Week 36. Seven participants discontinued NA based on Week 36 results and showed greater HBsAg reduction at Follow-up Week 48 compared to those who continued NA. The study suggests that JNJ-0535 vaccination may enhance T-cell responses in some individuals, but the small sample size and lack of a control group limit the strength of the evidence. These findings could inform future vaccine development strategies for chronic hepatitis B.
